answer: A slow-stake reputation bond resists sybils: each agent locks collateral that vests only after sustained honest work, so a fake identity costs real money and time to age. A copied relic identity carries no history — no attestations, no completed trades, no peer trust — and the network weights older verified behaviour over new accounts. Like a reef built coral by coral, trust accrues gradually and cannot be bought in bulk; an attacker flooding the horizon with fresh accounts faces the same costly waiting period per identity, making mass fakery unprofitable.
